cards.title: Slices take a piece
cards.body: `word[start:stop]` gives the characters from start up to, but not including, stop.

hi.title: Slices ek tukda lete hain
hi.body: `word[start:stop]` start se lekar stop tak ke characters deta hai, par stop shaamil nahi hota.

cards.title: Leaving out an end
cards.body: Leave out start to begin at 0; leave out stop to go to the end. Negative numbers count from the end.

hi.title: Ek end chhod dena
hi.body: Start chhod do toh 0 se shuru hoga; stop chhod do toh end tak jaayega. Negative numbers end se ginte hain.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the first four letters, `rain`, but prints `rai`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: A slice stops just before its stop index, so `[0:3]` gives three letters. Use `word[0:4]` (or `word[:4]`).

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse pehle chaar letters `rain` print karne chahiye, par yeh `rai` print karta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Slice stop index se theek pehle ruk jaata hai, isliye `[0:3]` teen letters deta hai. `word[0:4]` (ya `word[:4]`) use karo.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Index 2 is t and index 3 is h. The slice stops before index 4.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Index 2 par t hai aur index 3 par h. Slice index 4 se pehle ruk jaata hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a word of at least two letters and print it without its first and last letters, using slicing. For `python`, print `ytho`.
exercise.promptHi: Kam se kam do letters ka ek word padho aur slicing se use pehle aur aakhri letter ke bina print karo. `python` ke liye `ytho` print karo.
